usageNotes: Use this to provision a new QEMU/KVM virtual machine on a specific cluster node, or to restore one from a backup archive. The caller must hold VM.Allocate on /vms/{vmid} (or the target pool), Datastore.AllocateSpace on any storage used for disks, and SDN.Use on any bridge or VLAN referenced. The operation returns a task UPID string; poll the task API to determine when provisioning completes before attempting to start or configure the VM.

examples.summary: Create a Ubuntu 22.04 cloud-init VM with 2 vCPUs, 2 GiB RAM, a 20 GiB virtio-scsi boot disk, and a bridged NIC

tips: vmid must be unique cluster-wide and >= 100; use get_cluster_nextid to obtain a safe next ID before calling this.
When using 'archive' to restore a backup, VM.Backup permission is sufficient if the VMID already exists; VM.Allocate is required when creating a new VMID.
Use 'live-restore: true' with 'archive' to start the VM immediately while the restore streams in the background.
For UEFI/Secure Boot guests set bios=ovmf and include an efidisk0 with efitype=4m; omitting efidisk0 with ovmf will cause the VM to fail to start.
Cloud-init requires at least one ide/scsi/virtio drive marked as a cloud-init drive (via the Proxmox UI or a separate cloudinit drive param) and the 'agent' param enabled for best results.
Disk size shorthand uses GiB (e.g. 'local-lvm:20' allocates 20 GiB); the size sub-key inside the disk string is informational only and does not resize the volume.
